headline: The US open rally has fully reversed: S&P 500 down 1.2% in an hour

findings.headline: The open's relief rally is gone: S&P 500 back to flat on the day
findings.body: The S&P 500 fell about 1.2% in an hour, from roughly 7,411 at 15:30 to 7,320 at 16:30 Zurich, a 4-sigma move that wipes out the open's gain and leaves it level with yesterday's 7,323 close. The Nasdaq 100 slid by a similar amount, so the selling is in tech and AI, the same trade the open had bought back. VIX is only up to about 23.6 and gold, copper and the dollar are not signalling broad panic, so for now this reads as the open's bid failing rather than a macro shock. We did not find a single headline for the drop; it coincides with Anthropic becoming eligible to trade at 16:00 Zurich.

findings.headline: Philly Fed: orders fade while prices climb
findings.body: The Philadelphia Fed index fell to 6.3 from 20.9, far below the 17 to 20 expected, with new orders slightly negative for a fourth straight decline, yet prices received hit their highest since June 2022 and prices paid jumped 15 points. Jobless claims also beat forecasts at 203,000, and continuing claims rose 70,000 to 1.763 million, a sign that laid-off workers are taking longer to find jobs. That mix of softer demand and firmer pricing is the Fed's worst case, with a December hike already near-certain in futures, and equities are ignoring it for now.

findings.headline: Oil is pricing the Iran strike risk, not the inventory build
findings.body: Crude is firmer on reports that Trump is weighing another round of extensive strikes on Iran, with the White House asking the Pentagon how Iran might respond, while Tehran warned neighbours not to host US attacks. That is overriding a bearish EIA report showing a 3.4 million barrel US crude build against about 0.4 million expected. The December WTI contract also expires on Friday, so front-month moves into the close may exaggerate the signal.

view: Our view: the open's bounce has been fully sold, which confirms it was fragile and tied to one listing. We would wait to see whether the S&P 500 holds yesterday's 7,323 close and whether VIX stays near 23 before reading this as more than a failed rally.
